lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Unit performance task: reviewing a decision after the outcome

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic reviewing a decision after the outcome task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner reads a provided fictional multi-constraint scenario (a character choosing between two summer opportunities under a tight decision deadline, an uncertain final cost for one option, and no way to do both), works it to a defended decision with a documented fallback, presents that decision and reasoning to a guardian, and then reads a provided account of what happened afterward to review the outcome with the guardian.
safetyNotes: The scenario, decision, and outcome are all fictional; the guardian's role is to listen to the learner's reasoning and ask questions, not to grade the fictional character's choice.
The learner is not required to disclose any real personal decision as part of this task.

simulationAlternative.description: If a guardian is not available to hear the presentation and outcome review right now, the learner completes the full written performance task and outcome review independently, including a written self-assessment addressing the same questions a guardian's questions would raise, for guardian sign-off once available.

materials: adult-or-local: a guardian or trusted adult to present to

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l06-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l06-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l06-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l06-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Did the outcome match what you expected when you made the decision? What specifically was different, if anything?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u05-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Option generation and tradeoff analysis: At least three genuinely distinct options and a complete tradeoff table. | Fallback and guardian presentation: Fallback has a specific trigger, and the learner presented the full reasoning to a guardian. | Outcome review quality: Review states clearly whether the outcome matched expectations and why. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner and guardian identify which single piece of information, if the character had known it in advance, would have changed the decision, and discuss how the character could have gotten that information sooner.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic reviewing a decision after the outcome task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: 10–20 minutes for permission, required supervision or review, and physical-event attestation

resources.title: reviewing a decision after the outcome worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner reads a provided fictional multi-constraint scenario (a character choosing between two summer opportunities under a tight decision deadline, an uncertain final cost for one option, and no way to do both), works it to a defended decision with a documented fallback, presents that decision and reasoning to a guardian, and then reads a provided account of what happened afterward to review the outcome with the guardian.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact reviewing a decision after the outcome decision or action.
Model move 2: Before proposing any option, separate the stated problem from the underlying real problem, and name the three separate constraints (time, money, information) at play in the scenario.

Model move 3: Generate at least three genuinely distinct options (not variations of the same two choices), build a tradeoff table comparing them on the same criteria, and make and defend a decision using specific rows from your table.

Model check: Option generation and tradeoff analysis: At least three genuinely distinct options and a complete tradeoff table. | Fallback and guardian presentation: Fallback has a specific trigger, and the learner presented the full reasoning to a guardian. | Outcome review quality: Review states clearly whether the outcome matched expectations and why.

resources.title: reviewing a decision after the outcome action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for reviewing a decision after the outcome.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: reviewing a decision after the outcome coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner reads a provided fictional multi-constraint scenario (a character choosing between two summer opportunities under a tight decision deadline, an uncertain final cost for one option, and no way to do both), works it to a defended decision with a documented fallback, presents that decision and reasoning to a guardian, and then reads a provided account of what happened afterward to review the outcome with the guardian.
Coach direction: Before proposing any option, separate the stated problem from the underlying real problem, and name the three separate constraints (time, money, information) at play in the scenario.
Learner prompt: What is the real underlying decision the character has to make, separate from how the scenario first states it?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: reviewing a decision after the outcome complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Generate at least three genuinely distinct options (not variations of the same two choices), build a tradeoff table comparing them on the same criteria, and make and defend a decision using specific rows from your table.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I generated at least three genuinely distinct options, not variations of the original two choices.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I built a tradeoff table comparing all options on the same criteria.
Response 3 (t2-p3): State your defended decision and justify it using at least two specific rows from your tradeoff table.

Equal-access rule: If a guardian is not available to hear the presentation and outcome review right now, the learner completes the full written performance task and outcome review independently, including a written self-assessment addressing the same questions a guardian's questions would raise, for guardian sign-off once available.

resources.title: reviewing a decision after the outcome minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Did the outcome match what you expected when you made the decision? What specifically was different, if anything?

Success checks: Option generation and tradeoff analysis: At least three genuinely distinct options and a complete tradeoff table. | Fallback and guardian presentation: Fallback has a specific trigger, and the learner presented the full reasoning to a guardian. | Outcome review quality: Review states clearly whether the outcome matched expectations and why.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: reviewing a decision after the outcome supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l06-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g11-u05-l06-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional reviewing a decision after the outcome condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Option generation and tradeoff analysis: At least three genuinely distinct options and a complete tradeoff table. | Fallback and guardian presentation: Fallback has a specific trigger, and the learner presented the full reasoning to a guardian. | Outcome review quality: Review states clearly whether the outcome matched expectations and why..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l06-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
